D006-D005_h001.question:
Lately, things have been… off. It started about ten months ago, I think. I was buzzing, absolutely wired. I’d be up all night, sketching out new marketing campaigns, calling clients at 3 AM. I felt like I could conquer the world, like I was brilliant. My mood was all over the place, one minute I’d be ecstatic, the next I’d snap at anyone who looked at me funny. I’d start drafting a ton of listing agreements, then suddenly move to remodeling ideas for a client, then jump to redesigning my own website – couldn't finish a thing.

Then, around eight months ago, the visions started. I see people, shadowy figures mostly, just out of the corner of my eye. Sometimes they’re in my peripheral vision, and other times they just pop up in my living room. And the TV, the news anchors, they’re talking right to me, sending me secret messages through their gestures. My thoughts get so jumbled sometimes, I start rhyming words without meaning to, like "key and glee and set me free."

The past three months, though, have been the worst. All that manic energy completely drained away. Nothing brings me joy anymore. My biggest fear is driving, I keep having these sudden, terrifying urges to just swerve into oncoming traffic, or jump out of the car when I’m on a bridge. It’s terrifying because I don't want to die, but the impulses are so strong. It feels like the mania was just a blip, a brief, intense period, but these other… difficulties, they’ve clung on for so much longer.
D006-D005_h001.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D006-D005_h002.question:
It's been about ten months since things really started going downhill, doctor. I’m a police officer, you know, and just trying to do my job has become… impossible. I haven't been able to focus on anything at work, my mind is always racing and jumping from one thought to the next. One minute I’m buzzing with energy, feeling like I can take on the whole precinct, the next I’m snapping at my wife over nothing. It’s like there’s a constant buzz under my skin, and I just can't sit still.

Lately, though, some… stranger things have been happening for the last eight months. I keep feeling these creepy crawlies on my skin, like tiny insects, even when there's nothing there. And when I try to talk, sometimes the words just don't come out right. It's like my mouth is trying to speak a different language, and what comes out is just gibberish, and it's so frustrating because I'm usually so clear on the radio. It's like the world is ending, really, like a massive catastrophe is coming, and there’s nothing I can do to stop it. About three months ago, I just couldn't take it anymore. I felt so hopeless, had zero motivation for anything, and frankly, I tried to end it all. It’s hard to tell what’s real anymore. The manic episodes usually last for a few weeks, two or three, but these other… experiences, those have been a steady eight months now.
D006-D005_h002.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D006-D005_h005.question:
I’m Dr. Evans. What brings you in today?

"Honestly, doctor, it's all just... a lot. For the past eight months, I've noticed this really unsettling smell. It's like decaying flowers mixed with something metallic, and it can be so overpowering, sometimes it's all I focus on. And my thoughts have become so fragmented, my speech often comes out like 'the historical tapestry unravels, a gilded cage for forgotten echoes.' People just look at me blankly, and I can't seem to string a coherent sentence together.

It wasn't always this bad. About ten months ago, my mood started swinging wildly, from feeling absolutely elated, planning grand new exhibits for the museum – even for things not in our collection – to snapping at colleagues for the slightest thing. I'd be all over the place, unable to sit still, constantly pacing around my office, reorganizing things pointlessly. My attention just scatters like dust motes in a sunbeam; I can’t focus on anything for more than a few minutes. This really impacted my work; I couldn't even manage simple curation tasks. Lately, though, these manic-like periods have barely been there, just a blip here and there amidst all this other strangeness.

What's really been consuming me is this terrifying sense that the world is crumbling. Not just a feeling, but a deep conviction. It started around the same time as the smell and the confused talking, maybe eight months ago. I see the historical artifacts at work, and I feel this utter despair, convinced they're just vestiges of a world on the brink. Everything feels meaningless. And for the last three months, I've had no interest in anything anymore, not my research, not my collection, not even my cat. I just want it all to stop. I keep thinking, 'I want to die, I want to kill myself,' but I haven't made any plans. I just… I can’t live like this anymore."
D006-D005_h005.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

My thoughts jump around a lot, so much so that when I talk about one thing, I quickly switch to something completely unrelated.

I decided to renovate the whole house, started three new community initiatives, and somehow needed hardly any sleep, just pushing through the night. It felt incredible, like I was superwoman.
